purpose: Internal startup warm prompts. Not user requests and not formal performance inputs. Encoded with the adapter HF tokenizer using add_special_tokens=false.
c1_text: Internal startup note for the DeepInfer text service. The service starts one rank process for each of the eight devices. Each rank owns a complete native engine and a local scheduler. A request is added to exactly one rank, while the other seven ranks keep entering the same collective step loop and run the scheduler's placeholder work. Before the service accepts public traffic, the startup path performs two bounded internal checks. The first check sends one short request to a single rank. This exercises the all-rank and any-rank startup rules, the empty-rank placeholder path, and the first decode path on the owning rank. The second check sends one small request to every rank in the same scheduling round. Every rank then executes a real prompt step and a real decode step instead of dummy work. The internal checks use fixed text that is not taken from any user request, ignore the end-of-sequence token so the decode path runs to its configured cap, and are excluded from formal performance measurements. The service publishes readiness only after all eight ranks report idle with no active, running, or waiting requests. If either check fails or exceeds its deadline, the service does not listen for public traffic; it aborts the internal request, stops the rank group, and preserves the failure report for the next controlled restart. This note exists only to describe the startup contract and to provide a stable, valid prompt for the initialization pass.
c8_text: Startup verification note for the eight-rank batch path. In a coordinated batch, every rank receives one modest request before the group enters the next collective schedule. The rank scheduler therefore sees eight independent sequences with local prompt work on all devices. This is different from a single request, where seven ranks only execute placeholder work. The check covers the real prompt and decode path on every rank, including the speculative decode state, the variable-length verification path, and the graph replay used by the selected production configuration. The prompt is fixed internal text and is not a copy of a user question. The output cap is deliberately small, and end-of-sequence is ignored so that each request reaches the decode path instead of stopping after the first token. The check is not a benchmark and its latency is reported separately from public request latency. After the batch completes, the parent waits until every rank has flushed its outputs and reported an empty active set. Only then does the HTTP listener start and the readiness endpoint become reachable. A timeout or worker error leaves readiness unpublished and tears down the group through the normal shutdown path. The note is repeated here as a stable prompt for the batch initialization pass, and it contains no data from any customer request or private document.
